description: Hosted APIs and tools operated by Payload, organized by the problem they solve: x402 payment failure diagnostics, agent payment governance, and revenue entitlement verification, plus free CI checks. Payload's downloadable software is cataloged separately in products.json. Every price and limit below is stated as it operates today.

services.capability: Hosted diagnostic actions for x402 payment failures: diagnose, failure_classification, preflight, settlement_interpretation, resolve, duplicate_payment_risk, and recover. Each action returns structured evidence and an explanation of what failed and what to do next. A free quote endpoint returns the exact price before any payment.

free_entry.experience: npm package callx402 (v1.0.6): six free local MCP tools (x402_status, x402_diagnose, x402_evidence, x402_explain, x402_recover, x402_resolve). No account and no payment. Read-only and local; the tools never move money.
free_entry.paid_next_step: Hosted diagnostic actions run by Payload; the quote endpoint returns the exact price free before any payment.
free_entry.paid_price: $0.10 to $0.50 USDC per action (x402 on Base)
free_entry.proves: A structured local diagnosis of an x402 payment failure.

invocation.auth: none; the unpaid response is an x402 v2 payment requirement

invocation.note: Official MCP Registry listing. The npm package callx402 provides free local read-only tools, including x402_status.

services.limits: No guaranteed recovery and no diagnosis of every failure is promised. Settlement uses Payload's signed-redemption contract rather than the standard x402 facilitator flow. Actions named safe_retry, rescue, monitor, and execute are local-only and are not sold on the hosted rail.
services.name: callx402 hosted payment diagnostics

payment_flow.no_payment_alternative: The npm package callx402 ships free local MCP tools: read-only diagnostics that never charge and never move money.
steps: GET https://payload-rail.fly.dev/v1/callx402/quote returns the exact price for the action before any payment.
POST https://payload-rail.fly.dev/v1/callx402/actions/{action} without payment returns an x402 v2 402 challenge: USDC on Base (network eip155:8453), the amount, and the payTo address.
Pay the quoted USDC amount to payTo on Base from your own wallet. Payload never takes custody of your keys.

Redeem the original quote: resubmit with the payment tx hash and an EIP-191 signed authorization from the paying wallet, binding the wallet, action, tx hash, quote, recipient, network, and request inputs. A tx hash alone never authorizes an action.
The rail verifies the payment exactly once on-chain and returns the hosted diagnostic result.
payment_flow.summary: Quote first (free), then pay per action. Settlement uses Payload's signed-redemption flow, not a generic x402 facilitator, so facilitator-only clients cannot complete a hosted purchase.

payment_methods: USDC on Base via the x402 payment requirements returned by the endpoint

price.note: The exact per-action amount is quoted by the free quote endpoint and in the x402 payment requirements before payment.

services.capability: Hosted, non-custodial authorization and governance for agent payments: natural-language mandates compiled into spend constraints; an intent firewall returning ALLOW, DENY, or ESCALATE_HUMAN; per-transfer, payee, human-approval, and daily-budget policy enforcement; single-use passkey human approvals; signed-authorization verification; and fail-closed settlement reconciliation. Veyline does not provide custody, settlement, or execution.

free_entry.experience: Free sandbox tier: create a mandate and evaluate proposed agent payments before subscribing.
free_entry.paid_next_step: Developer or Production subscription via Stripe checkout on the product page.
free_entry.paid_price: Developer $99 per month; Production $499 per month
free_entry.proves: A signed allow, deny, or escalate decision for a proposed agent payment.

services.limits: An authorization layer does not guarantee protection against every attack or prevent every duplicate payment. Payload does not hold customer funds, and Veyline does not provide custody, settlement, or execution. Paid subscriptions are sold through a human Stripe web checkout; there is no machine-completable purchase path.

services.capability: Revenue rules engine: persistent Revenue Graphs encoding percentages, recoupment, waterfalls, caps, and attribution. Revenue events are applied against the current rule state, each participant's entitlement is calculated and written to a hash-chained, queryable ledger (exportable as JSON), and recorded payouts can be read back against what was owed. RevRule never holds, transfers, or distributes funds and never executes payments.

free_entry.experience: Browser sandbox running the real engine (labeled simulated; nothing moves money), plus a free self-serve console key for a caller's own graphs. Event simulation is a dry run that writes nothing.
free_entry.paid_next_step: RevRule license for production graphs and persistent production state, via Stripe.
free_entry.paid_price: $99 one time; the keyless public evaluate on the fixed demo graph is $0.01 USDC
free_entry.proves: Entitlements computed from the caller's own rules, ready to check real payouts against.

invocation.note: Free self-serve API key for a caller's own graphs
In-browser sandbox running the real engine. Simulated; nothing moves money.

services.limits: RevRule does not execute payments and never holds funds. It does not read or extract agreement documents, and it does not compare entitlements against external statements.
